title: Effects of a 12-week gait retraining program on the Achilles tendon adaptation of habitually shod runners
publisher: Scandinavian Journal of Medicine & Science in Sports
claims: Thirty male recreational runners who habitually wore cushioned shoes with a rearfoot strike were randomised to a retraining group (n=15) or a control group (n=15); 28 completed the study.
The retraining group ran in five-finger minimalist shoes with a forefoot strike pattern three times per week for 12 weeks.
After training, 57% (8/14) of the retraining group shifted from rearfoot to forefoot strike; all participants reduced their foot strike angle.
Achilles tendon length and cross-sectional area increased significantly in the retraining group, and Achilles tendon loading rate and peak force changed over time.
The authors describe the findings as preliminary evidence that a 12-week programme can strengthen the Achilles tendon for mechanical loading.
